author: buchanan_robert
text:
A woman, young and strong and fair
Went out to find her lover's lair;

And, finding none at home, she said:

"Ah well! I may not see him now,"
But still it grieved her heart to know
That he was gone away from her bow."

The poem “I Know Why The Caged Bird Sings” by Maya Angelou is about how an imprisoned bird has its wings clipped, so it can’t fly away from the cage and sing like other birds do outside. Though it feels caged, it knows that there are ways to get free (such as learning) if you put your mind to it.

author: buchanan_robert
text:
The night is dark and still, the city sleeps but for one—
A young boy sits alone, staring out into the gloom.

He sees nothing but darkness, all around him.

Suddenly, a sound echoes through the air—it’s as if something has come alive! A black shadow crawls along the walls…a sinister presence creeps closer…

“Mumma!” The boy calls softly “Where are you?” His voice trembles with fear. He watches the creature approach slowly; a large snake slithers towards him from nowhere at all – what could have caused such evil?

author: cushag
text:
A. The Road Not Taken (by Robert Frost)

Two roads diverged in a yellow wood,
And sorry I could not travel both
And be one traveler, long I stood
And looked down one as far as I could
To where it bent in the undergrowth;

Then took the other, as just as fair,
and having perhaps the better claim,
Because it was grassy and wanted wear;
Though as for that the passing there
Had worn them really about the same,

And both that morning equally lay
In leaves no step had trodden black.

text: The poet's language is more or less simple but it has an artistic flavor, and the lines are beautiful. There was no attempt at making the work difficult by using big words or archaic forms; instead the idea of the stanza is clearly brought out in its simplest form possible. The beauty of the poetry lies in the selection of words that are used for their meaning and not merely for sound effect. This kind of simplicity is also found in good prose. The green leaves droop, and the yellow light
Streams down through withered boughs that quiver;
But the red rose yet flushes on its stem
And smiles as though it would not die.

Oh I know, love is like this flower,—
It blooms with beauty for a while,
Then fades into decay!—its bloom no more
Is worth an hour’s pain to me.

It’s because they know me well,
That they don’t want their money held.
The wages are so small for such hard work,
They would go hungry without our offer!

Next year will bring enough for everyone—
At most, just one more week or two.

author: william_wordsworth
text:
(A) All we want is fair play:
For fair play,
 And to feel that the world understands us well.
 We are not so strong nor so brave as they;
 But our cause is their’s and theirs is ours—
 The great cause for which men have fought and died since history began!

author: buchanan_robert
text:
My friend has said that all his life,
He had not seen a day so bright;
It was like spring to him-so warm,
So full and strong, and sweet and wise!

But I remember quite as well
A time when nothing could be seen
Of bud or blossom on the trees,
And yet it seemed no longer night.

text:
My country’s star shines bright in the eastern sky,
 A beacon light guiding me through these changing times,
 It represents strength and unity, as nations unite to fight
 The forces of darkness that threaten our world today.
 My country will always have my heart and soul,
 Forever standing by its side no matter what may come our way.
 So let us hold fast together, for this shining light we see
 Will guide us safely home if only we can keep faith in eternity
